title: Australian property prices were flat in July, Sydney and Melbourne are now slightly negative for the year
excerpt: CoreLogic's national home value index was unchanged in July. Sydney and Melbourne are now marginally negative year-on-year, while Brisbane and Perth continue to lead growth.
body:
Australian residential property prices were flat in July, with the CoreLogic national Home Value Index unchanged over the month, according to fresh data released this week. The rolling annual rate of growth has slowed to 1.4% nationally, a sharp deceleration from the 8–10% pace of 2023 and 2024.

Sydney and Melbourne are now slightly negative year-on-year at -0.4% and -0.2% respectively. The growth story is concentrated in Brisbane (+5.1%), Perth (+7.8%) and Adelaide (+4.3%), where affordability relative to Sydney and Melbourne is still driving interstate migration.

Rents nationally rose 0.3% in July, the smallest monthly increase since early 2022. The annual rental growth rate of 4.8% is now below CPI inflation for the first time since 2021.
whatItMeans: Owner-occupiers: If you are planning to buy in Sydney or Melbourne, the market is currently flat-to-soft. There is no rush. Negotiate aggressively on price and conditions.
Upgraders: The days of 10% annual capital gains look to be over. Run the numbers on a 5- to 7-year hold, not a 2- to 3-year flip.

Investors: Rental growth is cooling and vacancy rates are ticking up in the inner-city apartment segment. The maths on negatively-geared investments has got harder, work the gross yield, not the headline price.
First-home buyers: The First Home Guarantee and state-based stamp-duty concessions have not changed. If you can service the loan, now is as good a time as any.
